title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is GTA 5 without the finesse - so why is the 2004 classic such a strange delight to return to?
text:
There is a place in Whitewood Estates where a promising stretch of blacktop suddenly gives way to the desert. It feels like the road has been erased, a sentence left unfinished. It's quietly strange, a weird bit of urban wrongfooting. But I guess it makes some kind of sense. California, after all, is home to California City, a town that was planned and then never really built. It sits out there now, north of Los Angeles, streets laid out but slowly being eaten by the sand and dirt. Still, 14,000 people lived there as of 2018. Design limitation or something stranger, this digital dead end is a reminder that all of this land, so modern, so ancient - all of this is spook country.

As for the XCOM series, the latest entry from Firaxis was 2020's XCOM: Chimera Squad, and before that was 2016's XCOM 2.

Firaxis was co-founded by Sid Meier in 1996, so 2026 is the studio's 30th anniversary. Take-Two bought the company in 2005 and put the studio and the franchise under the 2K banner.

title: 007 First Light Might Be The End Of The Line For James Bond’s Favorite Watch
text:
After months of searching and numerous potential frontrunners, Robert Pattinson has been cast as the next James Bond. It's lead to some questions about whether he's too famous or too old for the role, whether or not he looks like Bond, and just how different his portrayal might be to those that came before him. For some others, however, the questions is far more direct: What watch is he going to wear?

James Bond has long had recognizable brand associations, but one that has endured has been the partnership with luxury watch maker Omega. Bond was first seen wearing an Omega in 1995's GoldenEye, and was mostly recently seen sporting the latest iteration of the Seamaster Diver 300m in this year's 007 First Light. Although not a new film in the series, First Light still featured its own unique take on the Seamaster, the first ever created for a videogame, with Omega adding it to its bursting 007 collection that it makes available for purchase.

So given that it's been three decades, why could First Light be the last iteration of James Bond wearing an Omega? Simply put, Robert Pattinson doesn't wear one, and has very recently become a brand ambassador for one of Omega's Swiss competitors, Jaeger-LeCoultre. There's no confirmation that Pattinson's obligations will directly influence a brand deal between Omega and new Bond owners Amazon, but the omission of any watch at all in the announcement trailer sure has cause some speculation.

Daniel Craig, during his tenure as Bond, was Omega's chief ambassador, often wearing unreleased models to drum up interest for imminent releases. That might not be the case with Pattinson, which could suggest a change for what timepiece his Bond decides to switch to.

If Bond were to jump from Omega to JLC, it would be somewhat fitting. The watch maker manufactures some extremely elegant pieces with a rich history associated with each line. But none makes as much sense as the rectangular Reverso. The watch is distinct in its design, allowing the wearer to rotate the face and flip it 180 degrees, with a variety of designs on the back. Initially created for polo players to protect their prized wristwatches, you can clearly see a lot of potential for some weird and creative Bond gadgetry to intersect with a design like this.

Or maybe Pattinson will arrive on the block with yet another Seamaster Diver 300m, and all of this would've been wishful thinking. But if he doesn't, and this truly is the last we'll see of Bond with Omega, at least First Light introduced one of the better entries in the entire collection.

title: These Are Some Of The Biggest Snubs At The Game Awards 2026
text:
The nominees for The Game Awards have been announced. Some of the biggest games--and those that aren't out yet--make appearances on the list, including Grand Theft Auto 6 and Phantom Blade Zero, but some of the games could've--and maybe should've--been nominated in multiple categories. So, let's go over some of the biggest subs at this year's TGAs.

Let's start with the big one: Game of the Year. You've got six games nominated here: 007 First Light, Control Resonant, Grand Theft Auto 6, Phantom Blade Zero, Resident Evil Requiem, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. All of them are fabulous and well-deserved, but a couple of games are missing: House House's co-op adventure Big Walk and Rebel Wolves' vampire RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker. They appear elsewhere, sure, but I think they deserve GOTY contention, as well.

Let's move onto Best Performance. You've got some stellar voice work here: Angela Sant’Albano as Grace Ashcroft in Resident Evil Requiem, Liam McIntyre as James "Logan" Howlett in Marvel's Wolverine, Manni L. Perez as Lucia Caminos in GTA 6, Patrick Gibson as James Bond in 007 First Light, and Rahul Kohli as Arjun Devraj in Saros. Not taking anything away from these incredible voice talents, but Nick Apostolides as Leon Kennedy in Resident Evil Requiem, Sean Durrie as Dylan Faden in Control Resonant, and Will de Renzy-Martin as Coen in The Blood of Dawnwalker deserve some recognition, too.

Marathon could've easily been nominated for Best Art Direction and Best Action Game. Overwatch and WoW/WoW: Forever would've made sense in the Best Ongoing Game category. Denshattack's soundtrack is too good not to be nominated for Best Score and Music. And Castlevania: Belmont's Curse could slot into a number of categories, including Best Action/Adventure Game, Best Art Direction, and Best Narrative.

There are probably many others that have come out this year that maybe could--and maybe should--have been nominated but weren't for one reason or another.

Regardless, we won't have to wait too long to learn what games win what categories, as The Game Awards will air live on December 10 at 4:30 PM PT / 7:30 PM ET.

title: What Does It Take For World Of Warcraft To Be Nominated At The Game Awards?
text:
The nominees for 2026's The Game Awards have been revealed, and just like every year before it, there is a glaring omission in the Best Ongoing Game Category: World of Warcraft.

This year's nominees are Arc Raiders, Fortnite, No Man's Sky, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, and Final Fantasy 14 Online. Of particular note is Square Enix's MMORPG, which has been nominated in the category every year since 2021. Developer Blizzard's MMO, on the other hand, is nowhere to be seen. 

WoW is among the most popular live-service games in industry history and has been for 22 years. Blizzard releases new expansions for its MMORPG every other year like clockwork and has done so for over two decades. It reintroduced the old-school version of the MMO, WoW Classic, in 2019 to huge acclaim from the game's passionate community.

In the years that followed, it continued to add new expansions to the modern version of WoW, adding highly requested features like account-wide unlocks and new endgame solo content. For WoW Classic, it re-released past expansions, added official servers and support for a permadeath mode popular among the game's community, and ran experimental seasons that added new content to the classic version of the game. Taken all together, the various versions of WoW have millions of players.

Earlier this year, Blizzard released Midnight, the latest expansion for modern WoW that added player housing to the MMO for the first time. A few weeks ago, it released WoW: Forever, the third major version of the MMO. Built on the bones of WoW Classic, Forever is intended to be an ongoing game that will add new content and changes to the old-school version of WoW, existing alongside the modern game. Forever was the biggest launch in WoW history in terms of concurrent players, Blizzard said.

Yet, since 2017, WoW has never even been nominated in Best Ongoing Game, a category that serves to put a spotlight on titles that continue to receive new content and evolve the experience over time--something Blizzard wrote the book on with WoW.

WoW being omitted this year in particular is more baffling than any time before, as Blizzard not only released a brand-new expansion, but also an entirely new version of the game that players have dreamed about for years. On the other hand, Final Fantasy 14's new expansion, Evercold, doesn't release until 2027, even if the game has received significant content updates over the course of the year. 

Even other Blizzard games have been nominated in this category multiple times over the years. Overwatch won Best Ongoing Game in 2017 and was nominated again in 2018. Diablo 4 earned a nomination in 2024 with the release of its first expansion, Vessel of Hatred. 

Meanwhile, it seems like nothing WoW does is enough to warrant attention. There is, of course, a simple answer to why this seems to be the case--nobody, or at least very few, on the The Game Awards voting jury plays, or keeps up to date, with WoW.

That's a shame, because if there was any year where WoW deserved to be nominated, it's this year. Forever is the culmination of an entire community's dream of having an ongoing, new version of classic WoW, and Midnight continues the philosophy of player-friendly changes first added in 2024's The War Within expansion. There are now more ways to play WoW than ever before, each receiving unprecedented support and updates. In fact, players in the modern version of WoW have been complaining that there's perhaps too much to do and that content updates are maybe too frequent. 

This is all to say that it feels like WoW deserves just a little recognition. It's been running for over two decades at this point, and in that time has in many ways defined what an "ongoing game" is and can be. 2026 has been a banner year for WoW, and its future is looking brighter than ever. It deserved a moment in the spotlight. Maybe next year (though I wouldn't bet on it).

title: GTA 6 Leads TGA Nominations, And Reviews Aren’t Even Live Yet

On top of being spotlighted for Game of the Year, the game also has nominations for Best Art Direction, Best Audio Design, Best Game Direction, Best Action/Adventure, Best Narrative, Best Performance (for Manni L. Perez's portrayal of Lucia), and Best Score, bringing the crime sim's total nominations to eight.

We already knew GTA 6 would be eligible for this year's ceremony. After all, per the TGA FAQ, the cutoff date for eligibility is November 20, one day after the game comes out. With a "jury of over 100 global media and influencer outlets" selecting the nominees, and many of these folks likely having plenty of hands-on time with Rockstar Games' latest release, it isn't much of a shocker to see GTA 6 at the top spot. Still, it is a little awkward that it has so many nominations before its release that may reveal what to expect from the critical reception..

Maybe it shouldn't be too surprising or weird, though. After all, the game isn't officially out yet, and it's already sold approximately 16 million copies and generated nearly $2 billion in revenue. Maybe that expensive sick day caused by the GTA Flu won't be so expensive.

title: Xbox Game Pass Gets Even More Games In November
text:
The second half of November is usually quiet for several reasons when it comes to new game releases–and one other big reason–but Xbox Game Pass subscribers can look forward to several new titles to close off the month--and eight games will also be leaving Game Pass on November 30.

Microsoft has announced a handful of new additions to the Game Pass library, including a kid-friendly game to kick things off and a sneak peek at some sporty fun for the first week of December. These announcements typically come in two waves, with a sneak peek split between them, so this list isn't complete yet.

The first game on the way is Paw Patrol: Dino World. Ideal for younger members of the family who definitely shouldn't be playing GTA 6 right now, this family-friendly game revolves around the PAW Patrol working together to round up lost and scared dinosaurs.

Other highlights this month include Call of the Elder Gods for a Lovecraftian puzzle-adventure, High on Life 2 joining Game Pass Premium, and Roadside Research, which is all about aliens trying to run a gas station while poorly disguised as humans.

title: Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Breaks His Silence, Says He Would Come Back
text:
Jensen Huang, the co-founder of Nvidia who was recently ousted as CEO after he admitted to having an affair with someone that US intelligence believes could by a spy for China, has now said he is open to returning to the company.

In his first public statement since his resignation from Nvidia, Huang told The Wall Street Journal that he is aware of the "outpouring of calls" from Nvidia employees, investors, business partners, and customers for him to come back as CEO. He would come back, if asked.

"If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO," he said.

This statement came a day after a source told CNBC that the Nvidia board is not considering bringing Huang back as CEO.

Huang released his statement on social media, saying, "Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me."

His statement added: "I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. Nvidia has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like Nvidia be possible. I love our country, and I love Nvidia."

Huang acknowledged that he "did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia" and owned up to making "serious mistakes in my personal life." He said he created problems for Nvidia's Board of Directors and he said he "deeply" regrets that. "I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation," he said.

Nvidia was the world's biggest company by market cap until the company's stock price began to crash in October, and it fell further after the controversies came to light, including multiple affairs beyond the one with the alleged spy.

To be sure, Nvidia remains a juggernaut--it's currently the No. 2 biggest company in the world, with a market cap of $3.75 trillion. Only Apple, with a market cap above $4 trillion, is bigger than Nvidia.

The New York Times and other media outlets reported that Huang had a romantic relationship with the former CEO of the AI company Megaspeed, Alice Huang (no relation). US intelligence sources claim that Alice Huang was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, though China officially denies this narrative and says it's an effort by the US to smear China.

Megaspeed, for its part, said Alice Huang left the company in 2025 and denied any wrongdoing in the Nvidia scandal.

The Nvidia controversies have led to turmoil in the stock market, in part because Nvidia is one of the "Mag 7" companies that are driving growth in the US. Some of the information coming to light suggests that Nvidia's accounting and export control compliance are not buttoned up, and this has fueled further concerns about the growth potential and returns on investment for the AI trade. Numerous other technology and AI stocks have dropped in value significantly since the Nvidia news broke.

Nvidia's interim boss is CFO Colette Kress, who is expected to lead Nvidia's earnings call today, November 17. The earnings report will be closely watched and highly scrutinized--keep checking back with GameSpot for the latest.

title: GTA 6 Has A Lot Of Different Bird Species, Here’s How Many
text:
Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has a lot of details and depth, including dozens of different bird species for people to find. If you're a birder, you're in for a good time.

According to The Guardian, Rockstar confirmed that there are 62 types of birds that players can spot. Players can whip out binoculars to "study" birds and animals like they could in Rockstar's last game, Red Dead Redemption II.

As PC Gamer reminds us, Florida is home to more than 500 bird types, so GTA 6 will have just a fraction of the different kinds of birds people can find in real Florida. GTA 6 was never going to replicate every single bird, of course.

Some of the birds that are found in Florida, and probably GTA 6 as well, include flamingoes, spoonbills, wood storks, egrets, kites, terns, and scrub jays. Florida is also home to bald eagles, and we'd expect them to show up in GTA 6.

Inclusive of birds, GTA 6 has more than 170 animal types, including cane toads, alligators, manatees, and rhesus macaque monkeys.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game launches at midnight local time, so it will be playable for people in New Zealand and Australia very soon. You can switch your Xbox region to New Zealand to play early, if that works.

title: An NES Power Glove Just Became The Most Dangerous Weapon In Pro Wrestling
text:
All Elite Wrestling's recent Full Gear event had no shortage of great moments, but Austin Creed stole the show with a move straight out of Street Fighter. After teaming up with his Next Level partner Kofi Kingston and Swerve Strickland to take on Bandido, Hangman Adam Page, and Brody King in a Texas Death Match, anything went in this brawl — including vintage NES accessories.

Looking the worse for wear at King's hands, Creed busted out an NES Power Glove and landed a Shoryuken uppercut that exploded in a shower of sparks, knocking his burly foe flat on his back. The moment quickly went viral, and Creed's team would eventually triumph, emerging as the AEW World Trios Champions.

Creed is no stranger to video games; during his run with WWE, he ran the Up Up Down Down YouTube channel, where he competed with fellow performers in a wide variety of games. Wrestling and video games have formed a symbiotic relationship over the years, with top performers like Kenny Omega referencing games like Street Fighter and Final Fantasy 7 for his signature moves. Video games have also positively influenced professional wrestlers, with top WWE star Roman Reigns saying it's a popular downtime activity with his fellow wrestlers and better than some of the "extracurricular" exploits of previous generations.

In another video game crossover, former WWE champion Cody Rhodes played Guile in the live-action Street Fighter movie, which was released last month, and he even cosplayed as the character at WWE SummerSlam. Sadly, the film wasn't a big box-office hit, making only $100.7 million worldwide during its run (via Box Office Mojo). In comparison, the other Capcom-based movie, Resident Evil, was far more successful, generating over $416 million worldwide and making it the highest-grossing Resident Evil movie of all time.

title: New Ubisoft Boss Wants Studio To Become “A24 Of Video Games”
text:
Ubisoft recently hired games industry veteran Christoph Hartmann to become the general manager of Creative House 2. In a new interview, Hartmann talked about his hopes for the unit, saying his dream would be for it to become "like the A24 of video games."

He told Variety that what he means by this is that Creative House 2 can be like A24 in that it can make games that are both critically and commercially successful. A24's biggest hit ever was this year's Backrooms, which made more than $400 million worldwide against a reported budget of $10 million and was received positively by fans and critics.

Some of A24's other recent big critical and commercial hits have included Marty Supreme ($192 million), Everything Everywhere All at Once ($148 million), The Drama ($135 million), and Civil War ($127 million).

Saying Ubisoft's Creative House 2 could aim for what A24 is doing is certainly an ambitious goal, and it's not the first time that Hartmann has made such a bold claim about what he's working on. When he was at Amazon, Hartmann said his objective was to help Amazon become “the Disney of the future,” with gaming standing alongside TV, film, music, and retail.

Creative House 2 covers franchises like The Division, Ghost Recon, Splinter Cell, and March of Giants (which Ubisoft bought from Hartmann's previous company, Amazon). "Hartmann’s role is to oversee strategic direction and development of the studios and brands under Creative House 2," Ubisoft said.

Hartmann told Variety that he wants Creative House 2 to "definitely not" be a place that only makes shooter games.

"I want us to be a label which really looks after the core gamer. And what I mean by that, it’s almost easier to describe what we’re not going to do. So I’m not going to do a racing game. I’m not going to do sports. I’m not going to do a casual kids title. But could we do an RPG one day? Could we do MMO? Could I maybe do even a strategy game? Sure, it’s all coming down to the right talent," he said.

Hartmann also discussed why he left Amazon, saying the company is focused on the AI buildout right now and "games just can't be their prime focus right now." Prior to Amazon, Hartmann worked at 2K for decades.

title: Ocarina Of Time Is 2026’s Best-Selling Physical Game In The US, But GTA 6 Is Coming
text:
Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 is the best-selling physical game of 2026, according to Circana, but GTA 6 is coming out soon and could topple that record.

Circana's Mat Piscatella said the Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 was the first game to surpass 1 million physical units sold in the US for its launch week since 2023's The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.

Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 released on November 5, and Circana's reporting period ended on November 7, so the achievement was actually accomplished in just two days, not even a full week.

Ocarina of Time's physical edition, which includes a cartridge, sells for $70, compared to $60 for its digital counterpart.

GTA 6 launches on November 19, and while the game is fully digital, Rockstar is releasing a "physical" version of the game at brick-and-mortar retailers. Buyers don't get a disc--only a code for the game.

In any event, for Circana, code-in-a-box games are considered new physical game sales, so GTA 6 is no doubt going to topple Ocarina of Time's record.

Ocarina of Time's remake for Switch 2 sold more than 5 million copies over its first four days globally. The latest sales data for GTA 6 pre-purchases show that the game has passed 16 million units sold worldwide.

title: GTA 6 Nearing 16 Million Copies Sold And Passes $1.5 Billion In Revenue
text:
The video game research company Sensor Tower has updated its GTA 6 sales tracker to reveal the latest, albeit unofficial, sales data for the open-world crime game. According to Sensor Tower, GTA 6 has now sold 15.88 million total units via pre-purchases, which works out to about $1.54 billion in gross revenue.

The report said PS5 sales are dominating the mix, with GTA 6 selling 11.83 million units on PS5 so far, compared to 4.04 million on Xbox Series X|S. That means of the 15.88 million GTA 6 sales so far, 75% are on PS5 and 25% on Xbox Series X|S.

In total, GTA 6 sales for PS5 have so far reached $1.15 billion in revenue, compared to $390 million for Xbox Series X|S. Sony and Microsoft keep about 30% of revenue due to their platform fees, so GTA 6 being a huge success directly benefits both of those companies.

The huge gap in sales between platforms is not surprising because the PS5 is dominating Xbox Series X|S in terms of console sales. In fact, GTA 6 is breaking records on Xbox, Microsoft has said, and the sales numbers for GTA 6 on Xbox line up with Xbox's share of the console market.

Sensor Tower is projecting as many as 25 million total pre-purchases for GTA 6 by launch, and if the 75/25 split holds, that would be about 18.5 million units on PS5 and 6.5 million on Xbox Series X|S.

GTA 6 is the most preordered game of all time for PlayStation and Xbox. If the 10 million pre-purchase number is real, that would break a record for most preorders set by Cyberpunk 2077 (8 million).

Sony holds the marketing rights for GTA 6 on PS5, but that doesn't mean that Microsoft is doing nothing to try to promote the game. Just recently, Microsoft announced a GTA 6-inspired custom Xbox console that sits inside an alligator.

Circana has released new data that shows that GTA 6 holds 29% purchase intent among US console and PC gamers. That means nearly 1 in 3 console and PC gamers in the US plan to buy GTA 6–this is the highest purchase intent that Circana has ever measured for any game.

GTA 6 may indeed be a gigantic hit commercially, and one that helps lift the entire industry with increased sales of hardware and accessories. But anyone looking to buy a new console to play GTA 6 is set for major sticker shock, as consoles today are more expensive than ever. Not only that, but GTA 6 is not going to save the industry’s many serious and deep-rooted issues, experts believe.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game's file size is about 212GB, and thankfully, preloading is already underway. The game unlocks on November 19 at midnight local time, and that means US players will be among the last in the world to get in.

People in New Zealand, meanwhile, will be the first in the world to play GTA 6. If you're thinking about booking a flight to the land of Hobbits, here are some tips for packing your PS5 safely.

title: Sony Is Updating The PS5 Again, And It Might Have GTA 6 Pirates In Mind
text:
A new PS5 firmware update has dropped, but even at a chunky 1.2GB download, version 26.07-14.23.00 doesn't include a comprehensive list of notes.

"We've made some security fixes to the system software," the very short update notes read. Notably, this is the fourth PS5 firmware update since October 1, and typically there's a buffer period of several months between downloads. While Sony hasn't confirmed it, the current thinking is that the company is shoring up its defenses for the release of GTA 6 to prevent the game from being pirated.

The new firmware will be mandatory for new game releases as well, including GTA 6, which means that PS5 hackers and homebrew hobbyists have their work cut out for them. The hacking scene recently made big advances on the console, jailbreaking systems that have update 14 and below installed, and thus allowing more pirated games to be played. Sony is under pressure to prevent GTA 6 from being pirated, and with the PS5 console holding the lion's share of GTA 6 preorders, there's plenty of financial incentive to keep the game secure on that platform.

Security researchers and hackers have been leveraging generative AI and automated decompilation analysis to discover lower-level system vulnerabilities and dump game binaries much faster, creating an arms race between Sony and hackers.  Every time a potential vulnerability or homebrew exploit surfaces--like the recent vulnerabilities that targeted PS5 consoles running 13.60 and 14.22 firmware--Sony rushes out a mandatory console patch to plug the hole.

Beyond security measures, we've also seen base PS5 consoles updated with Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR), which is also rolling out to more games. An AI-based upscaling technology derived from the PS5 Pro's PSSR, it initially supported only Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei.

title: GTA 6 Has Teamed Up With The Weather Channel To Show How Dynamic Leonida Can Be
text:
Rockstar Games has found an unexpected partner to show off one of GTA 6's most impressive features: The Weather Channel. The US broadcaster has shared an exclusive look at Leonida's weather system via six new screenshots and forecasts that make the fictional destination sound like somewhere you'd need to check the weather before visiting.

It's an unusual collaboration, but a very fitting one. GTA 6 takes place in Leonida, a fictional state inspired by Florida, where sunshine, torrential rain, thunderstorms and tropical storms are all part of the ecosystem. Who better to show off the unpredictable climate than The Weather Channel?

The broadcaster posted the collaboration on X, writing "Nobody knows weather like we do. That's why Rockstar gave us an exclusive look at the forecast for Leonida and the dynamic weather in GTAVI."

Instead of just posting the six new screenshots, The Weather Channel provided six different weather reports for the various locations across Leonida. Each has its own conditions and some local facts, making the entire post sound like a genuine forecast.

The reports include heavy rain reducing visibility across the Keys, a thunderstorm rolling over the swamps of Pelican Valley--and obscuring some feisty "nippers" at the same time--and sea fog threatening to obscure the expensive beachfront views at South Ocean Beach. There's also a tropical storm making the waters around the Rusty Anchor particularly choppy, and Gambit Bay has a low-lying morning mist ahead of hunting season.

One forecast warns commuters traveling from Key Lento to expect more rain and wind. It seems like an almost mundane detail for a game about a pair of criminals, but it's this exact impressive world-building that makes Leonida feel real.

The six new screenshots are especially impressive, showing off the towering storm clouds and lightning strikes through to dense fog that makes entire stretches of the coastline disappear. Rockstar isn't treating weather as just a visual effect--it will have a real impact on the way you play the game.

Owen Shepherd, Rockstar's VP of Art: Light and Rendering, explained that the studio had to completely reimagine its in-game weather systems to make them feel "more localized, persistent, and above all dynamic." He added that Leonida's weather can range from clear blue skies to towering cumulonimbus clouds, reflecting the unpredictable conditions of the real-world Florida climate.

The emphasis on localized weather is interesting. Instead of having the entire map experience the same conditions, Leonida's different environments can have their own atmospheric conditions. A coastal resort might be swallowed by fog, while a storm rolls over the wetlands in the distance. This approach will make exploring the enormous map feel different depending on when and where players visit. The screenshots don't confirm how individual gameplay mechanics will be affected, but they offer a deeper look at the environmental detail Rockstar is aiming for.

There's something pretty extraordinary about a real-world weather broadcaster getting involved in the marketing of Grand Theft Auto--and it really puts into perspective how the arrival of GTA 6 is a once-in-a-generation event.

GTA 6 launches on November 19, but players in New Zealand will be able to get their hands on the game ahead of the rest of the world, thanks to hitting midnight before anywhere else. For unrelated reasons, if you want to set your Xbox region to New Zealand, we've got you covered.

title: How To Play GTA 6 Early On Xbox Using This Trick
text:
Due to GTA 6's non-simultaneous release, people in New Zealand will be the first in the world to play the highly anticipated open-world crime game when it releases at midnight local time there.

If you want to become a Kiwi for a day and you plan to play on Xbox, you can trick your console into thinking it's in New Zealand to play early.

The following trick has worked before, but there is no guarantee that it will work for you this time with GTA 6, or you might not want to do it at all. After all, Microsoft's own policy says people should only change their region if they have moved to a different country or are already in a new region.

If that all sounds OK to you, here's how to change your Xbox region to New Zealand (via Insider Gaming).

  • Go to Settings
  • Click System, then Language & Localization
  • Switch your location to New Zealand
  • Restart your console

The process of changing regions on PlayStation 5 is not as straightforward and involves numerous other steps--Insider Gaming has a rundown. However, it's also been reported that players changing their PS5 region have begun receiving account suspensions without warning.

GTA 6 launches on November 19, but midnight in New Zealand on November 19 is 3 AM PT / 6 AM ET on November 18. So people in the US will have to wait a very long time to play GTA 6 compared to the people who live in New Zealand.

title: Delete GTA 6 For A Chance To Win Another Game

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 finally releases this week. The game looms so large that other companies are using it to market their own games, including Devolver Digital.

title: The Head Of GTA 6’s Parent Company Helped Make One Of The Best Christmas Movies Of All Time
text:
One of the most memorable and beloved Christmas movies is 1990's Home Alone, but it almost didn't happen, and the head of GTA 6's parent company played a role in bringing the movie to market.

Strauss Zelnick, the current CEO of Rockstar Games owner Take-Two, was the president and COO of 20th Century Fox at the time--he was among the youngest-ever Hollywood CEOs at the age of 32.

Warner Bros. was originally backing Home Alone and had actually begun production on the movie until budget concerns prompted the studio to pull the plug. "Four days into production, they shut down the picture and canceled it. That never happens," Zelnick told David Rubenstein.

Fox, under the leadership of chairman Joe Roth and Zelnick as president, swooped in and gave the filmmakers--including director Christopher Columbus and writer John Hughes--the money to make Home Alone.

That turned out to be a fantastic investment for Fox, as Home Alone ranked as one of the top five highest-grossing movies of the year in the US. It grossed more than $476 million globally against a $13 million budget, and it picked up two Oscar nominations. Home Alone also helped launch the career of Macaulay Culkin, and his role of Kevin remains his most memorable part.

So why didn't Zelnick keep making movies?

Zelnick was on top of the world as a film executive after Home Alone. However, he said he saw a bright future in the interactive entertainment business, so he left Fox in 1993 to join Crystal Dynamics where he served as president and CEO.

"I left Fox voluntarily, which no one ever does, to move to Silicon Valley, take a 95% pay cut and become the pre-revenue CEO of a little tiny video game company called Crystal Dynamics in 1993," he said in the Rubenstein interview.

After Crystal Dynamics, Zelnick shifted to the music business in the role of CEO as BMG Entertainment from 1994 to 2000. During that time, BMG started a gaming unit, BMG Interactive, which published the original GTA in 1997.

After that, Zelnick and an investor group took over Take-Two, which was in a tough financial spot at the time and was sued by the US government for accounting fraud.

Since the takeover, Take-Two has thrived. Its share price exploded from about $10 in 2007 to more than $220 today, and Take-Two today has a market cap of over $40 billion. The GTA franchise is a juggernaut at Take-Two, but it actually only accounts for 15% of the company's revenue in a non-release quarter. Take-Two today owns and operates a number of big non-GTA franchises, including NBA 2K, Borderlands, Mafia, BioShock, Civilization, and more.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. It's reportedly already sold close to 15 million copies and generated nearly $1.5 billion in revenue.

title: WoW: Forever’s Dungeons Have Gotten Yet Another Big Change
text:
World of Warcraft: Forever's dungeons have changed once again, with developer Blizzard's most recent adjustment requiring an emergency hotfix to address players' outcry.

Dungeons, specifically how much experience points players earn from them, have been one of Forever's most debated topics going back to the game's beta. Make them too lucrative, and players will just stay inside dungeons instead of questing out in the world. At the same time, Blizzard doesn't want dungeons to be one-time affairs, with players completing all their quests in a single run and never going back.

Blizzard opened a new front in the dungeon wars on November 13, making a change so that nobody in a dungeon group would receive any experience if enemies were considered "trivial" to to any player in the group. The idea behind this appeared to be an effort to prevent high-level players from running low-level ones through dungeons, in the process curtailing players from selling character "boosting" services to lowbies.

Unfortunately, far too many players playing the game normally were caught in the crossfire. Many of Forever's dungeons have double-digit level ranges, meaning even if a player might find enemies early on in the dungeon trivial, enemies and bosses later on won't be. It also created a scenario where players were leveling up mid-dungeon, only to suddenly find themselves fighting trivial enemies and bricking the experience gains for everyone in the group.

As it turns out, committing to a multi-hour adventure, only to suddenly find nobody is earning experience points and everyone is mad at you because you happened to level up, is not a great social experience. Blizzard was at least quick to admit the change "missed the mark" and made adjustments a day later on November 14.

"With hotfixes that are now live, we've just deployed a further change to this restriction, making it so the XP nullification only kicks in when the high-level player is more than 12 levels above the level of the enemies," Blizzard said in a forum post. 

At least judging from forum comments, that seems to be a more reasonable compromise, even if it still does prevent higher-level players from coming to help their lower-level friends.

It's just the latest chapter in what has become one of the biggest ongoing discussions in the Forever community. During the Forever beta, Blizzard made changes to experience earned from dungeon quests, nerfing them significantly. 

Come launch day, it became apparent Forever's dungeons weren't worth running more than once, as after completing quests, experience earned from kills was extremely low. Blizzard agreed, and issued a change on November 8 to increase the amount of kill experience earned in dungeons by 50%. It was a sizable increase, but is still lower than the experience amount players earned from doing dungeons in WoW Classic.

Forever's launch broke WoW concurrent-player records, and after one week of adventuring through Azeroth once more, classic WoW feels fresh again. Despite the record-breaking launch, Blizzard hasn't released official stats, but fansites have already pieced together the game's most popular class, race, and faction.

title: GTA 6 Should Help Boost PS5 And Xbox Sales, But Their Astronomical Prices Could Hurt
text:
Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19, and it's expected to help boost console sales for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. But the uptick in hardware sales might not be as dramatic as you might think--and there is a good reason why.

According to Circana's Mat Piscatella, there will be "probably" be a boost to PS5 and Xbox Series X|S sales when GTA 6 comes out, but the uptick could be muted due to the recent PS5 and Xbox Series X|S price hikes. Piscatella said anyone who is excited for GTA 6 and needs a new console might think twice when they see how astronomically expensive new consoles have become today.

Historical prices

When GTA 5 launched in 2013, the average price paid for a new PS3 was $252 and the Xbox 360 was $232. Adjusted for inflation, that would be $363 for the PS3 today and $334 for the Xbox 360. Those prices are significantly below the average price of a new PS5 ($646) and Xbox Series X|S ($663) today.

"Not a good thing"

Earlier this year, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick, who oversees the company launching GTA 6, said, "The rising cost of hardware is not a good thing." At the same time, Zelnick isn't worried about the impact on GTA 6, in part because he believes the game is so good that people will find a way to pay for a new console.

 "However, a lower price point for hardware would be a good thing because there’d be more hardware in people’s hands," he said. "Probably the most relevant thing is the world continues to move to open systems, and that will continue.”

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. People in New Zealand get to play first, and if you're planning a trip to the land of Hobbits, here are some tips for safely packing your PS5.

title: EA Begs You To Not Delete Madden 27 For GTA 6
text:
We all know what's coming: Grand Theft Auto 6. Whether you're ready for it or not, the most anticipated game of the decade is preparing to launch on November 19, and ahead of its release, EA is begging you to please not ditch footballs for guns.

According to Push Square, EA added a "don't delete" pop-up message to Madden NFL 27. The pop-up says there's an update coming to the football simulator on November 17, just before GTA 6 drops.

"Don't delete," the message reads. "[Encrypted Signal] The target is locked. The crew is assembling for a high-stakes run. Await the signal from our insider on 11/17 ... do not leak this transmission!"

In a November 10 post on Madden NFL 27's official X account, EA said that a throwback Madden 97 update is coming on November 18 with old-school playbooks, 16-bit gameplay, and the All '97 Team. Underneath that post, EA had asked that you stick around a little while longer.

This is in reference to the humongous amount of storage space that Rockstar Games' GTA 6 will take up when it launches. Start clearing out your hard drive now because you need at least 212GB of free space to download GTA 6. In comparison, Madden NFL 27 needs approximately 60GB to install the game.

If you're like me and you still have the base PS5, this means you have approximately 667GB of usable space. Sure, you can fit both GTA 6 and Madden NFL 27 on the same console. However, if you have any other recent releases like The Blood of Dawnwalker (~50GB), Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen (~81GB), Phantom Blade Zero (~135GB), and Valor Mortis (~60GB), then you can see how quickly you'll run out of space--especially since you have to leave a little wiggle room for game updates, too. That's not to mention the games dropping in 2027, such as Final Fantasy VII Revelation, which game director Naoki Hamaguchi said could be around 200GB.

EA has recently gone through a restructuring that saw 400 employees across the company get let go and the legendary studio BioWare get shut down. In the midst of this, the publisher reiterated its commitment to the Madden franchise with a new title currently codenamed Project Gridiron. While filled with potential, we do fear that EA's plan for the series may lean into everything that the company itself does wrong.

title: Rockstar Could Have Released GTA 6 Sooner As GTA 5.5, But “You Have To Take Big Swings”
text:
After years of development, multiple delays, and loads of hype, Rockstar Games is finally releasing Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 19. What took so long?

According to Rockstar publishing executive Jennifer Kolbe, the team at Rockstar "could have made GTA 5.5, and done it faster." However, "Ultimately, that's not what they wanted," she told The Guardian.

Rockstar boss Rob Nelson, meanwhile, said it was important for the studio to go above and beyond with GTA 6, and that takes time. "You have to take big swings. It can’t be just more of the same," he said.

GTA 6 looks to be a big step up from GTA 5 in a number of ways, including the visuals and technical improvements. Beyond that, the story this time around is a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style narrative about a crime-loving couple--Jason and Lucia. It's also the first time Rockstar is releasing a GTA game with a playable female protagonist.

GTA 6 took so long to come out because Rockstar is seeking "perfection," according to Take-Two. “The team at Rockstar really does seek to do something that’s never been done before. That’s really hard and it takes a long time,” he said.

Rockstar and its owner, Take-Two, stand to benefit greatly from what's expected to be a commercial blockbuster with GTA 6. But could future GTA game releases come at a faster pace? According to Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick, the "nature and velocity" of GTA releases will look "dramatically different" over the next decade, but he didn't share more or commit to any specific timelines.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. People in Australia can attend a funeral at KFC to get the day off work to play it.

GTA 6 unlocks at midnight local time and not simultaneously around the world. This means people in the US will be among the last in the world to get to play.

title: NBA 2K27’s GTA 6 Crossover Includes A Whole GTA-Inspired Limited Edition Of The Game
text:
Ahead of the GTA 6 release this week, publisher Take-Two Interactive and 2K Sports have announced an NBA 2K27 crossover with the game. Starting November 27, Vice City will take over the digital basketball courts, and a special-edition NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition will also be released to promote GTA 6.

The $80 digital-only NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition features Miami Heat player Bam Adebayo on the cover, and for that GTA 6 touch, the art also includes the signature Vice City neon glow. This is something of a first for Take-Two Interactive--and possibly, the rest of the industry--as releasing a special edition of a game that promotes another game isn't something that we've seen before. This version also includes bonus Vice City-themed content and several benefits for GTA+ subscribers.

For Season 3 of NBA 2K27's live-service league, Vice City-themed content and rewards across The City social hub and MyTeam mode will be available to unlock. This three-week promotion will include bonuses and access for GTA+ Members, and Take-Two says players can expect themed apparel, including Vice City and Los Santos jerseys, Burger Shot and Cluckin' Bell Employee Outfits, and more.

Vice City-themed limited-time events will run throughout the season, with players competing in Conquer Leonida and Vice Run. Wednesdays will offer a chance to earn extra reputation by wearing Rockstar Games collaboration gear in Wear & Earn events, and one of the new modes is Neon vs. Noir, a 5v5 full-court clash pitting a Vice City team against a Los Santos lineup. MyTeam will also feature Vice City-themed cards, a powerful new Premier Exchange card, and limited-time modes.

The new gear will cost you some bucks, as the Season 3 Pro Pass--which offers access to the premium track with Vice City rewards like the Burger Shot gear, Cluckin' Bell outfit, Cactus Jack jersey, and Macca the Gator--will cost $10. The Hall of Fame Pass, which includes everything from the Pro Pass, 10 instant Level Skips, an extra 15% XP booster, and 15,000 VC, is priced at $20, and to get all the GTA-themed cosmetics, you have to grind through the 40-level season track. If you purchase the Vice City edition, the Season 3 Pro Pass is bundled with your copy.

GTA+ members on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S can also play the standard edition of NBA 2K27 for free from November 27 to January 15, 2027. If they like what they see, they'll get 20% off the game if they choose to purchase. GTA 6 preorders also include a one-month trial of GTA+.

Finally, GTA+ members can also download a Vice City bonus content pack featuring a Vice City-styled blue boat hat and oversized T-shirt, 30 skill boosts for five games, and 15 Gatorade boosts for five games.

GTA 6 marketing has been heating up as the game gets closer to launch, and this isn't the only basketball promotion on the table. For one night only, the NBA's Miami Heat will wear GTA 6-inspired jerseys when they host the Milwaukee Bucks on November 18, and the match will take place on a court inspired by Vice City.

title: Shooting Suspect In Custody After Opening Fire Near Xbox Dev’s Studio
text:
A drive-by shooting in Southern California ended with no injuries and an arrest after the gunman reportedly opened fire near a business and office campus that houses Xbox subsidiary InXile Entertainment.

According to Aftermath and local affiliate KTLA5, the shooting occurred on November 11 at an office building on the former Marine Corps Air Station in Tustin, California. The police department posted on Facebook that, after uncovering "multiple shell casings in the area," local detectives worked "around the clock" to locate the suspect.

Sergeant Christopher Peterson told Aftermath on November 13 that although the investigation is still ongoing, an unnamed suspect had been apprehended "less than 48 hours" after the shooting.

"Officers got there [on November 11]," Sergeant Peterson said. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why."

An InXile Entertainment spokesperson corroborated the incident with Aftermath, expressing relief about the situation.

"We're relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office,” the spokesperson said. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate."

Founded in 2002, InXile Entertainment has been under the Xbox Game Studios umbrella since 2018. Since its founding, the studio has developed several games, from the 2004 ARPG The Bard's Tale to the 2011 action-adventure Hunted: The Demon's Forge to the 2014 post-apocalyptic RPG Wasteland 2. Currently, the team is working on Clockwork Revolution, a steampunk ARPG not too dissimilar from immersive sims like BioShock and Dishonored. It has no release date right now, but InXile Entertainment is targeting a 2027 window for PC and Xbox Series X|S.

title: We Got A Grand Theft At Disney World Before GTA 6
text:
The "We got X before GTA 6" meme continues as a Grand Theft has been reported at Walt Disney World's Epcot theme park just days before Rockstar's open-world crime game releases, and the meme comes to an end.

The Walt Disney World: Active Calls account, which tracks police reports in the Disney World area, said a Grand Theft call at Epcot came in at 9:52 PM on November 14.

There are no further details to go on here, but Grand Theft, known as Grand Larceny in some states, involves stealing something valuable. Epcot and Disney in general has lots of items that would be considered valuable.

This is the closest that Disney World might come to GTA 6, as Rockstar already confirmed that GTA 6 won't have its own version of the park. That makes sense, too, considering Walt Disney World is located in Orlando and GTA 6 takes place in its own version of Miami, which is more than 200 miles away.

Calls for Grand Theft are not uncommon at Disney World. In October 2026 alone, the County Sheriff's Office received at least seven Grand Theft calls.

One of the most infamous heists at Walt Disney World took place at Epcot. In 2018, thieves nabbed the multi-hundred-pound Buzzy animatronic from the Cranium Command attraction, which was housed at Epcot's shuttered Wonders of Life pavilion.

It has never been recovered. A documentary, Stolen Kingdom, was released in 2025, chronicling the heist and the wider black market for Disney props.

More recently, the Paddlefish restaurant at the Disney World entertainment district, Disney Springs, was robbed by someone who swam up to the waterside restaurant in frogman gear, forced two workers into a corner, obscured the security camera with foam, and made off with cash. This case has not been solved.

In other Disney news, the entertainment giant is teasing "major" announcements for The Game Awards next month. As for GTA 6, the game finally releases on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

The "We got X before GTA 6" memes have been among the most popular and hilarious over the years as fans waited and waited for the game to release. Even Take-Two's own CEO, Strauss Zelnick, is aware of the memes.

title: GTA 6 Promo At KFC Is A Fake Funeral So You Can Take The Day Off To Play
text:
The popular fried chicken chain KFC has announced a frankly absurd GTA 6 promotion: a fake funeral so people have a “legitimate” excuse to take the day off to play Rockstar’s latest.

The fake funeral for a woman, "Ann Alibi," will take place Thursday, November 19 at 11 AM at KFC Robina in Queensland. People can attend in person or watch the funeral by livestream. The local restaurant is part of a region of Australia known as the Gold Coast, which KFC says is the equivalent of GTA 6's Vice City (which itself is a stand-in for Miami).

"The service will include a hearse, coffin, floral tributes, a book of condolences, an order of service and even a heartfelt eulogy delivered by a surprise guest. All the appropriate arrangements for a fitting farewell," KFC said.

The restaurant is also handing out free fried chicken to anyone who shows up in person. For those who can't make the services, KFC will offer free delivery through its app across Australia on November 19.

Anyone planning to eat fried food and play video games should be mindful of what might happen to their controller ... unless you got your hands on the limited-edition "greaseproof" controller that Microsoft put out years ago. Check out the video below to see how an Xbox controller holds up to heavy grease.

A KFC spokesperson said of the GTA 6 promo, "We appreciate that Australians have responsibilities, but some occasions are simply too important to miss. And in accordance with Ann's final wishes, we've made sure the funeral takes place during working hours."

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. People in Australia will be among the first in the world to play it since the game unlocks at midnight local time and not simultaneously around the world. title: Xbox Is Looking For Smarter Ways To Stop Its Next Console From Costing A Fortune
text:
No one knows yet exactly what the next-gen Xbox console, Project Helix, will be, but most people are convinced it won't be cheap. The ongoing memory shortage has driven current-gen console prices skyward since 2024, with the Xbox Series X rising from $500 in 2020 to $800 in 2026. Project Helix is projected to cost as much as $1,800 at launch, but Microsoft aims to keep the price down when it eventually releases the device.

According to VP of next-gen Jason Ronald, techniques like neural rendering could help manage costs. "It's definitely a challenging time, but as a system and a platform designer, it's also one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable," Ronald said in the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine. "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years."

In a nutshell, neural rendering uses AI to predict and generate high-quality video game frames while using only a portion of hardware power, similar to upscaling technoligies like PSSR, DLSS, and FSR. This could enable next-generation visual leaps while keeping the console accessible and reasonably priced for consumers. The other benefit is that the AI software models can improve over time through updates, as console hardware remains fixed over its lifespan, hence Ronald's quote about improvements reaching Project Helix over a few years into its run.

It remains to be seen how these breakthroughs will be spread across Project Helix, which Ronald teased as a family of devices that can address home, mobile, and cloud gaming needs. Xbox suggesting that it's working smarter to deliver an affordable gaming experience is an idea that Shawn Layden touched on recently, as the former PlayStation boss spoke about how Sony should be less concerned with chasing improved graphics and rather focus on making a cheaper PS5-level console instead.

Meanwhile, Sony is squeezing more life out of the PS5 generation with AI-guided upscaling technology, and the base model PS5 got its own version of this in the form of Quick Spectral Super Resolution. Originally available for only two games, QSSR is coming to more titles in the future, like Control Resonant, Arc Raiders, and No Man's Sky.
